## TL;DR

Muse Code (`muse` 1.4.x) is wired as a RepoOS harness through `muse exec --json`. The driver parses the MSP JSONL stream, mints a UUID session id (the only shape Muse accepts), resends trust and approval flags on every process, keeps the sandbox on, and uses SIGTERM to cancel. Token counts come from the terminal `run.usage` record; cost is absent, so it stays unknown. Official certification and the budget allowlist stay on the human follow-up (#1039), with `verifiedAt` left null.

## Work and rationale

This turn did not reimplement the driver. The implementation was already committed on `feat/add-muse-code-meta-coding-harness-driver`, and main (including the AGENTS.md pressureGuard wording fix) was already merged. The job here was to confirm the build, run the scoped gate once, and request handoff if that gate passed.

The adapter follows the contract in `docs/agent-compatibility.md` rather than inventing a second session protocol. Every managed turn — engineer, resume, and one-shot advisory roles — goes through one flag set: `--json`, `--trust-workspace`, `--approval-mode never`, `--max-model-steps`, an optional `--session-id`, and `--model` from config. Muse does not remember options between processes, so omitting any of those on a later turn would silently change behavior. `--trust-workspace` is required because a live run without it loaded the worktree as untrusted (no AGENTS.md, rules, or skills). `--yolo` is deliberately not used: it would also turn the sandbox off. Approval mode `never` is the unattended path with the sandbox left on, and `engineerPermissionGaps` treats a missing `--approval-mode` as a real gap so a future edit cannot drop it unnoticed.

Session continuation is `--session-id` with a UUID RepoOS generates. Muse rejects the deterministic `repoos-<task>-<role>` ids that pi uses (exit 2). The same flag both creates and resumes; a second `exec` with the same UUID returned the same stream id on a live run, which is the proof the parser keys off. Invalid ids are never passed.

Advisory turns (PM, reviewer, CTO) add `--disable-write` and `--disable-shell`. A live write attempt was refused and created nothing. The tradeoff is documented rather than papered over: a Muse PM cannot run `repoos` itself, and a Muse reviewer cannot run `git diff` or tests. File reads still work, and RepoOS applies output through its own patch path.

Cancellation stayed on the default SIGTERM. A live long run stopped promptly with no leftover children, so there is no Crush-style SIGINT special case.

Usage is recorded from the terminal `run.usage` payload (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `calls`). Even a trivial prompt reported tens of thousands of input tokens because Muse sends its own system prompt and tool definitions — the same class of profile Crush has, not a parser bug. There is no cost field, so the Tokens view shows tokens with cost unknown. Tool cards use `task.lifecycle.side_effect_intent` plus `tool.result`; argument payloads are not on the stream, so cards show name and output only. Model discovery has no `muse models` subcommand; the driver pins a fixed list (default `muse-spark-1.3`) and the contract notes `muse model-profile show`. `--reasoning-effort` exists on the CLI but RepoOS has no per-task reasoning path, so runs keep the CLI default.

Live probes that settled those questions (shape, resume, read-only refusal, SIGTERM, UUID rejection, untrusted workspace) are written in the Muse section of `docs/agent-compatibility.md`. They are driver research, not certification. The probes stayed inside the authorized budget: spark model, a three-step cap, throwaway temp directories, sandbox on, and no credential material copied into fixtures or docs.

Tests cover the argument shape with a fake binary rather than another live call: UUID versus rejected id, the shared flag set on fresh and resume launches, advisory `--disable-write` and `--disable-shell`, and the JSONL parser against the envelope kinds a real run produced (`run.terminal.completed`, `run.usage`, side-effect intents, tool results). Streaming text is held back when a fragment might still complete a runner signal, then released without the signal, matching the other drivers that scan assistant prose for handoff markers. Worktree placement is the existing-worktree flag or the process cwd, so the agent edits the task tree RepoOS already created instead of opening a second one. Model and step-cap values are launch arguments only; nothing is written back into Muse's own config.

## Approaches tried

Reusing pi's deterministic session id was the natural first shape and is wrong for this CLI: Muse exits 2 unless the id is a UUID. The driver mints `randomUUID()` only for Muse and still shares the "session id both creates and resumes" launch path with pi.

A Crush-like SIGINT cancel was the other fork. The live SIGTERM run reaped the process without orphans, so the contract keeps the default signal instead of a Muse-only override.

`--yolo` would have made unattended runs simpler and was rejected because it disables the sandbox. The task required `--approval-mode never` with the sandbox left on.

## Challenges and blockers

Muse's JSONL is an MSP envelope (`stream`, `payload_type`, `payload`), not the event names neighboring drivers use, so the parser had to be written against the generated schema and then checked against a real 1.4.14 stream. Tool arguments never appear, which limits transcript cards.

Read-only advisory mode cannot host the usual PM/reviewer shell steps. That is recorded as a product tradeoff, not hidden behind a fake success.

Certification, a budget-allowlist entry, and `verifiedAt` are out of scope. They need a human probe under #1039. This session did not claim them.

The scoped check is the remaining gate for this turn. A stale-build skip is not a failure: `bun run build` reported the sources unchanged. Only failures caused by this branch's diff should be fixed before handoff.

## Key learnings

Harnesses in this family often bill a large prompt-token floor on a one-word reply because the vendor system prompt and tool list ride along. Treat that as expected once a live `run.usage` line shows it.

Flags that are "sticky" in a TTY are not sticky across `exec` processes. Resend trust, approval, step cap, model, and session id every turn.

Session-id alphabets are part of the adapter contract. A shared id helper that assumes `repoos-<task>-<role>` will fail closed on Muse; UUID validation belongs next to the flag builder.

Research runs and certification are different records. Leave `verifiedAt` null when the runs only answered driver questions.
